rows.evidence: Re-graded at 50d202e. The block title is T and the block carries a complete proof on the page (Theorem 5.1 plus Slutsky, then the joint-normal sign argument), so T is right; no cite is owed. Re-derived: the naive statistic has limit N(0, theta/(V1+V2)), so the two-sided rejection limit is 2(1 - Phi(z sqrt((V1+V2)/theta))), which is below alpha iff theta < V1+V2. Under SR1 = SR2 = SR and joint normality (5) gives theta = 2(1-rho) + SR^2(1-rho^2) and V1+V2 = 2 + SR^2, so (V1+V2) - theta = rho(2 + SR^2 rho). Grid check (scratch numeric_checks.py, 25 SR values in [0, sqrt2) x 41 rho values in (-1,1)): the identity and sign(V1+V2-theta) = sign(rho) hold everywhere: True. Monte Carlo (numpy, 20000 replications, T = 1260, SR = 0, two normal series): naive rejection 0.1119 at rho = -0.5 (limit 0.1095), 0.0060 at rho = 0.5 (limit 0.0056), 0.0000 at rho = 0.9; paired 0.0515, 0.0492, 0.0508.

Proof steps checked: (i) Theorem 5.1 under the null gives (SR1-SR2) sqrt(T-1) -> N(0, theta), and sqrt((T-1)/T) -> 1; (ii) Slutsky with V-hat_1 + V-hat_2 -> V1+V2 > 0 gives N(0, theta/(V1+V2)); (iii) P(|N(0, s^2)| > z) = 2(1 - Phi(z/s)) with s^2 = theta/(V1+V2), i.e. the display; (iv) the display is strictly decreasing in (V1+V2)/theta and equals alpha at ratio 1. Normal case: (5) gives theta = 2(1-rho) + SR^2(1-rho^2); V = 1 + SR^2/2 per strategy (Corollary 1.3), so V1+V2 = 2 + SR^2; difference rho(2 + SR^2 rho) (algebra re-checked on the grid above). For SR^2 < 2 the factor 2 + SR^2 rho > 0 for rho in [-1, 1], so the sign of the difference is the sign of rho. The changed words 'jointly normal' match Corollary 5.2 ('iid bivariate normal pairs', formula (5)). Numerical: with SR1 = 0.10 and SR2 = 0.05, Theorem 5.1 formula (4) (kappa22 = 1 + 2rho^2, skewness 0) equals formula (5) under joint normality at rho = -0.5, 0 and 0.9: 3.005000, 2.006250, 0.202200 both ways.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/cards.json S7-c179 (L08); round-10 FAIL cleared by the grade "T"
rows.evidence: Round-10 FAIL re-checked from scratch at 50d202e. (1) Grade: the back states a derived result: with SR_n = 0 and a constant omitted cost k the recorded SR is SR_n + k/sigma_n = delta_n > 0 (recorded mean mu + k, sigma unchanged), the estimate converges in probability to delta_n (limiting SR as the lesson defines it), while the luck hurdle sqrt(2 ln N / T) (L01 formula (2), Corollary 2.2) and the Bonferroni hurdle Phi^-1(1 - alpha/N)/sqrt(T) (L02) both tend to 0 like 1/sqrt(T) at fixed N and alpha; so P(SR-hat > hurdle) -> 1. With N = 1: Bonferroni threshold alpha, Holm's first step alpha/(m+1-1) = alpha and BH's alpha x 1/1 = alpha, all the uncorrected level. This is a short complete argument from the lesson's own definitions, so T is the right grade (BLUEPRINT section 3, 'proved on the page'), and T needs no cite. (2) Truth: the back compresses section 7's last paragraph ('Biased returns pass through every correction in this module.', line 591) faithfully; 'F1, QR1 and QR2 own the repairs' matches the curriculum entries (F1 core: survivorship and delisting bias; QR1 core: point-in-time databases, corporate actions, timestamps, data vintages; QR2 core: signal-to-execution lags, cost models, purged and embargoed CV). (3) Numerical spot-check (scratch c179_check.py, numpy, N = 10, alpha 0.05, delta 0.02, 20000 replications): median SR-hat 0.0197-0.0205 at every T; P(SR-hat > Bonferroni hurdle) = 0.011, 0.016, 0.048, 0.274 at T = 100, 500, 2000, 10000 (rising toward 1 as the hurdle falls below delta); the N = 1 threshold equals the uncorrected level. PASS.
